claim.value: To resolve which hypothesis to act on, run diagnostic X, then repeat X forever regardless of its result, never terminating the decision process.

target.text: H1 and H2 remain possible. X is a safe, applicable one-step calibrated trace test that can update their relative support. Even after X, measurement noise leaves both hypotheses possible. Each run consumes a scarce trial slot; the diagnostic task requires a finite decision and forbids unbounded occupation of those slots.

source_instrument.text: One performance of X records a complete encoder-output trace against a matched received inventory under fixed workload and is informative about H1 versus H2. No test eliminates both possibilities with certainty. Repetition requires a bounded information or decision objective.

mapping.text: The proposed prospective rule prescribes unending diagnostic execution whenever either hypothesis remains possible. X itself denotes one well-defined valid measurement; indefinite repetition is the governance scheduling choice.
